questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum required front setback for a residential house in an Open Market subdivision?
questions.n: PD 957 mandates a minimum 3-meter front setback to ensure adequate space between the dwelling and the road right-of-way.

questions.q: What is the maximum percentage of the gross area that can be utilized as 'Saleable Area' in a PD 957 subdivision project?
questions.n: PD 957 limits the saleable area to 70% to ensure 30% is reserved for roads, open spaces, and facilities.

questions.q: For a 'Medium Cost' subdivision under PD 957, what is the minimum lot area required for a single detached house?
questions.n: PD 957 specifies 100 square meters as the minimum lot size for single detached homes in the Medium Cost category.

questions.q: In a corner lot, what is the standard measurement for the 'chafer' or cut-off at the intersection of the property lines?
questions.n: A 4-meter chafer is required to ensure visibility for drivers and safety for pedestrians at road junctions.

questions.q: What is the minimum floor area for a dwelling unit in an 'Open Market' subdivision project?
questions.n: PD 957 requires a minimum of 42 square meters of gross floor area for Open Market housing units.

questions.q: What is the required minimum lot frontage for a duplex or semi-detached house in an Open Market development?
questions.n: An 8-meter frontage is required for duplex/semi-detached homes in the Open Market category.

questions.q: Which of the following is TRUE regarding firewalls in PD 957 developments?
o: A firewall must have a minimum 2-hour fire-resistive rating.
Openings like windows are allowed if they are small.
Firewalls do not require a permit if they are under 2 meters high.
Firewalls can be built on all four sides of the property.
questions.n: The material must be able to withstand fire for at least two hours to protect the adjacent property.

questions.q: For 'Medium Cost' row houses, what is the minimum required lot frontage?
questions.n: PD 957 sets 3.5 meters as the minimum frontage for Medium Cost row houses.

questions.q: What is the minimum side and rear setback for a Medium Cost residential project under PD 957?
questions.n: Both Open Market and Medium Cost projects require 2-meter side and rear setbacks.

questions.q: Which of these is considered 'Non-Saleable Area' in a subdivision plan?
questions.n: Parks, playgrounds, and roads are non-saleable areas intended for community use and circulation.

questions.q: For a PD 957 subdivision with a size of 1 hectare or less, what is the minimum required width for the Main Road?
questions.n: For the smallest scale of PD 957 projects, the main road is permitted to be 8 meters wide.

questions.q: What is the minimum thickness for a concrete road pavement in a PD 957 subdivision?
questions.n: PD 957 standards specify 150mm as the minimum thickness for concrete road slabs to ensure durability.

questions.q: If a subdivision density is 100 units per hectare, what is the minimum percentage of gross area required for Parks and Playgrounds?
questions.n: 3.5% is the requirement for a density of 150 units per hectare and below.

questions.q: Which government agency is currently responsible for the issuance of the Certificate of Registration and License to Sell for PD 957 projects?
questions.n: The Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD) now oversees the functions of the former HLURB.

questions.q: What is the minimum required width for a 'planting strip' on a road with a 15-meter Right-Of-Way (ROW)?
questions.n: PD 957 mandates a 1.3-meter planting strip for roads that have a 15-meter total width.

questions.q: In PD 957, what is the maximum length of a 'Cul-de-sac' road?
questions.n: The IRR specifies 120 meters as the maximum length to ensure fire trucks and service vehicles can maneuver safely.

questions.q: What is the minimum requirement for the water supply system in a PD 957 subdivision?
o: Shared deep well for every 5 lots
Connection to a public water system or a community system
questions.n: PD 957 requires a centralized or public connection to ensure a reliable and safe water supply for all residents.

questions.q: Which of the following describes a 'Block' in subdivision planning?
o: A parcel of land bounded by streets or natural features
The area designated only for commercial use
The total area reserved for parks
questions.n: A block is defined as a land area surrounded by streets, roads, or natural boundaries like rivers.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the maximum length of a block before it must be intercepted by an alley or path?
questions.n: Blocks exceeding 400 meters are generally discouraged and require an alley at the midsection for accessibility.

questions.q: For a PD 957 row house cluster, what is the maximum number of units allowed in a single row?
questions.n: PD 957 limits a single row house cluster to 20 units before a mandatory gap is required.

questions.q: In a PD 957 subdivision project with a gross area of 30 hectares and above, what is the required minimum width for the Main Road?
questions.n: For large-scale developments of 30 hectares and above, the main road must be at least 15 meters wide to handle high traffic volume.

questions.q: Which of the following is the minimum required width for a 'Service Road' in a PD 957 development?
questions.n: The minimum width for a service road, which typically provides access to individual lots, is 6 meters.

questions.q: What is the minimum sidewalk width required for a road with a Right-of-Way of 12 meters?
questions.n: For a 12-meter ROW road, PD 957 specifies a minimum sidewalk width of 1.3 meters.

questions.q: In a Medium Cost subdivision under PD 957, what is the minimum lot area for an 'Irregular' shaped single detached lot?
questions.n: The shape of the lot does not reduce the minimum area requirement; it must still meet the 100 sqm standard for Medium Cost.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum distance between the property line and the curb for a 'Major Road' (Planting Strip + Sidewalk)?
questions.n: For major roads (12m-15m), the combined width of the planting strip and sidewalk starts at 2 meters or more.

questions.q: What is the minimum required pavement material for roads in a PD 957 subdivision?
questions.n: PD 957 mandates durable all-weather surfaces, specifically concrete or asphalt, for all subdivision roads.

questions.q: For a subdivision with 200 lots per hectare, what is the required percentage of gross area for Parks and Playgrounds?
questions.n: At a density of 200 units/ha (which falls in the 196-225 range), 9% of the area must be open space.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the required capacity for a water tank if a community system is used?
o: Average daily demand plus fire reserve
questions.n: The system must be able to supply the total daily need of the residents plus a dedicated volume for fire protection.

questions.q: What is the maximum allowed grade (slope) for a road in a PD 957 subdivision?
questions.n: The IRR generally limits road gradients to 12% to ensure vehicle safety and proper drainage.

questions.q: How long is the 'Validity of the License to Sell' under PD 957?
o: Until the project is completed or revoked
questions.n: The License to Sell remains valid for the duration of the project's development until it is finished or the DHSUD revokes it for violations.

questions.q: What is the minimum vertical clearance for an overhead power line crossing a road in a PD 957 project?
questions.n: A minimum clearance of 5.5 meters is required to ensure that all standard vehicles can pass safely beneath power lines.

questions.q: In the absence of a public sewer system, what is the mandatory requirement for sewage disposal in PD 957?
questions.n: If a centralized treatment plant isn't feasible or available, each unit must have its own septic tank that meets health standards.

questions.q: What is the minimum distance for a 'dead-end' street before a 'turn-around' (Cul-de-sac) is required?
o: No minimum; every dead end needs one
questions.n: Any road that reaches a dead end and is longer than 120 meters must provide a turn-around area for safety.

questions.q: Which document must a developer post to guarantee the completion of the subdivision's infrastructure?
questions.n: A Performance Bond (in the form of cash, surety, or real estate mortgage) is required to ensure the developer finishes the project.

questions.q: In a PD 957 condominium, what is the minimum required floor area for a 'Studio' unit?
questions.n: For PD 957 (Open Market/Medium Cost) condos, the absolute minimum floor area for a unit is 18 square meters.

questions.q: What is the minimum width for an 'Alley' in a PD 957 subdivision?
questions.n: An alley, used to break long blocks or provide secondary access, must be at least 3 meters wide.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum requirement for 'Street Lighting'?
o: At every intersection and every 50 meters
questions.n: To ensure safety, street lights must be placed at all road junctions and at intervals of no more than 50 meters.

questions.q: What is the required minimum pavement for a 'Sidewalk' in a PD 957 project?
questions.n: Sidewalks must be paved with a non-skid material (usually concrete) to prevent accidents during rain.

questions.q: A developer wants to change the name of a subdivision after the License to Sell has been issued. What must they do?
o: Nothing; names can be changed anytime
Wait until the project is finished to update the name
Inform the buyers via a newsletter only
Apply for an Amended License to Sell from DHSUD
questions.n: Any major change, including the project name, requires an application for an amendment to the official license.

questions.q: What is the minimum radius for a 'Cul-de-sac' turn-around?
questions.n: The minimum radius for the turn-around area at the end of a dead-end street is 6 meters.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a requirement for an 'Open Market' subdivision?
questions.n: Under the Balanced Housing Development Act, the socialized component can be done offsite; it isn't a design requirement for the Open Market site itself.

questions.q: What is the minimum width of the ROW for an 'Entrance Road' of a subdivision regardless of its size?
questions.n: PD 957 generally requires the entrance road (the first stretch of road) to be at least 10 meters wide to ensure smooth entry/exit.

questions.q: In PD 957, what is the minimum distance between fire hydrants?
questions.n: Fire hydrants must be strategically placed such that no point is further than 125 meters from a hydrant (meaning a 250m max spacing).

questions.q: For a row house in an Open Market category, what is the required front setback if there is no parking provided onsite?
questions.n: The standard front setback for PD 957 remains 3.0 meters, regardless of the housing type (Single Detached vs Row House).

questions.q: What is the minimum required thickness for an 'Asphalt' road pavement in a PD 957 subdivision?
questions.n: PD 957 specifies 50mm as the minimum thickness for the asphalt wearing course.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what must a developer provide if they want to sell 'lots only' (no houses)?
o: A waiver for the buyer's right to water
A guarantee that the lot will double in value
Full disclosure of land use and restrictions
A sketch of a sample house
questions.n: For lot-only projects, the developer must clearly state the building restrictions and the type of units allowed on the lots.

questions.q: What is the minimum width for a 'Major Road' in a project between 5 to 10 hectares?
questions.n: For this size bracket (5-10 hectares), the main thoroughfare must have a 12-meter ROW.

questions.q: Which of the following is required for the 'Drainage System' in PD 957?
o: PVC pipes for all main lines
Surface runoff toward the street only
questions.n: The standard for drainage in PD 957 developments is an underground system using RCP to manage stormwater.

questions.q: What is the minimum size of a 'Community Center' (if required) for a project of 1 hectare?
questions.n: The requirement for community facilities like centers starts at 1% of the gross area for smaller subdivisions.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of row houses allowed in a 'cluster' before they must be separated by a side yard?
questions.n: A maximum of 20 row house units can be joined together; after this, a clear space (side yard) is required for fire safety.

questions.q: What is the minimum required width for a 'Minor Road' in a project sized above 10 hectares up to 30 hectares?
questions.n: For this larger project size, even the minor roads must have a 10-meter ROW to handle the expected internal traffic.

questions.q: Under PD 957, who is responsible for the maintenance of roads and open spaces until they are donated to the LGU?
questions.n: The developer is legally mandated to maintain all roads and facilities until they are officially donated to and accepted by the local government.

questions.q: What is the minimum 'Clearance' required for a residential unit's ceiling height in a PD 957 condominium?
questions.n: The minimum ceiling height for habitable rooms in a condominium is 2.4 meters.

questions.q: In a PD 957 development, what is the 'Rounding' or radius requirement for the curb at an intersection?
questions.n: Curb radii at intersections must be at least 6 meters to accommodate the turning path of most vehicles.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the required width for an 'Interconnecting Road' that links two different subdivisions?
questions.n: Roads intended to connect one project to another must be at least 10 meters wide to ensure adequate flow.

questions.q: Which of the following describes a 'Semi-Detached' unit in PD 957 terms?
o: A unit located on top of another unit
A house floating in the middle of a lot
A house with one side wall built on the property line
A house with firewalls on both sides
questions.n: A semi-detached unit (like a duplex) has one side wall sharing or touching a property line, while the other side remains open.

questions.q: What is the minimum depth for an 'Open Market' residential lot under PD 957?
questions.n: A common design standard to reach the 120 sqm requirement (at a 10m frontage) is a 12-meter depth.

questions.q: If a developer fails to complete the project on time, what can the DHSUD do under PD 957?
o: Take over the company and sell its assets
Nothing, as long as the developer is trying
Automatically transfer ownership to the buyers
Suspend the License to Sell and cease further marketing
questions.n: DHSUD can issue a Cease and Desist Order and suspend the license if the development timeline is not met.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the maximum number of storeys for a walk-up condominium?
questions.n: Condominiums up to 5 storeys can be classified as walk-ups; anything above this requires an elevator.

questions.q: What is the minimum thickness for a 'Sidewalk' concrete slab in a PD 957 subdivision?
questions.n: Sidewalk concrete slabs must have a minimum thickness of 100mm (approximately 4 inches).

questions.q: For a PD 957 subdivision, what is the required curb and gutter type?
questions.n: Standard concrete curb and gutters are mandatory to manage road drainage and protect the pavement edge.

questions.q: Which of the following is true about 'Firewalls' in row house construction?
o: They are only required on the front of the house
They can be made of wood if treated with chemicals
They must be at least 1 meter thick
They must extend 300mm above the roofline
questions.n: To effectively stop fire from leaping over the roof to the next unit, the firewall must extend at least 300mm (0.3m) above the roof.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the required distance between a residential house and a high-tension power line easement?
questions.n: A minimum 5-meter horizontal distance must be maintained from any structure to a high-tension power line easement for safety.

questions.q: What is the minimum required frontage for a row house unit in an 'Open Market' project?
questions.n: Open Market row houses must have a minimum frontage of 4.0 meters.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the minimum required width of a 'Minor Road' right-of-way?
questions.n: The smallest width for a Minor Road in a PD 957 development is 8 meters.

questions.q: What is the minimum thickness for a 'Sub-base' under a concrete road in PD 957?
questions.n: The sub-base (aggregate base course) must be at least 100mm thick to support the concrete pavement.

questions.q: When is a 'Certificate of Completion' issued for a PD 957 project?
o: When all roads, utilities, and facilities are finished according to the approved plan
Immediately after the License to Sell is issued
When the developer sells all the lots
After the first 10 houses are built
questions.n: DHSUD issues this certificate once all development works (roads, water, lights, etc.) are verified as complete.

questions.q: In a PD 957 subdivision, what is the requirement for 'Garbage Disposal'?
o: Every lot owner must drive their trash to the city dump
questions.n: The developer must provide a system or area for proper solid waste storage and collection.

questions.q: What is the minimum required width for the 'Carriageway' of a 10-meter road right-of-way?
questions.n: For a 10-meter ROW road, the actual paved road (carriageway) is typically 7 meters wide.

questions.q: What is the maximum 'Percentage of Slope' for a driveway entering a property from a PD 957 road?
questions.n: While the road limit is 12%, individual driveways are sometimes capped at 15% to ensure car chassis don't scrape.

questions.q: What is the primary law in the Philippines known as the 'Subdivision and Condominium Buyers' Protective Decree'?
questions.n: Presidential Decree No. 957 is the primary law protecting buyers in subdivision and condominium projects.

questions.q: Who is the person or entity specifically registered with DHSUD to engage in the business of selling subdivision lots or condo units?
questions.n: The developer is the entity that develops the project and is usually the one registered to sell the units.

questions.q: True or False: A developer can start selling lots even before obtaining a License to Sell from DHSUD.
questions.n: The law strictly prohibits any sale or offer for sale until a formal License to Sell (LTS) is issued.

questions.q: Which of these must be provided in every PD 957 subdivision regardless of size?
questions.n: A functional drainage system is mandatory for all subdivisions to prevent flooding and health hazards.

questions.q: What is the simplest definition of a 'Condominium' under the law?
o: A house built entirely of wood
An interest in real property consisting of separate occupancy of a unit and undivided interest in common areas
A large piece of agricultural land
questions.n: This captures the dual nature of owning a specific unit while sharing the rest of the building.

questions.q: When a buyer finishes paying for a lot, what document must the developer deliver to them?
o: A receipt for the last payment only
questions.n: Upon full payment, the developer is legally bound to deliver the Transfer Certificate of Title or Condominium Certificate of Title.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the 'Performance Bond' posted by the developer?
o: To guarantee that the project's infrastructure will be completed
To pay for the developer's vacation
To cover the electricity bills of the residents
To pay the marketing agents' commissions
questions.n: The bond ensures that if the developer fails, there are funds available to finish the roads and utilities.

questions.q: In subdivision marketing, any advertisement must be 'truthful'. If an ad says there is a 'Grand Park,' but none is built, who is liable?
o: The Newspaper that printed the ad
questions.n: The law holds the developer and owner accountable for any false claims made in their advertisements.

questions.q: What is the minimum required side setback for a residential lot under PD 957?
questions.n: PD 957 requires a minimum of 2.0 meters for the side and rear setbacks.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT allowed on a 'Firewall'?
questions.n: A firewall must be solid to prevent fire from passing through; openings are strictly prohibited.

questions.q: What is the official title of PD 957?
o: The Urban Development and Housing Act
The Subdivision and Condominium Buyers' Protective Decree
questions.n: This is the formal name of the decree intended to protect buyers from fraudulent practices.

questions.q: Which area in a subdivision is specifically intended for communal use and cannot be sold as individual lots?
questions.n: This includes roads, parks, and playgrounds which are for the common use of the community.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what must a developer obtain before they can invite the public to buy lots or units?
questions.n: The License to Sell (LTS) is the mandatory document issued by DHSUD that allows a developer to market and sell.

questions.q: If a developer makes a promise in a brochure (like a swimming pool), what does PD 957 say about it?
o: The developer is legally bound to provide it
Only if it is written in the notarized contract
The buyer should have checked if it was true
It is just for illustration purposes only
questions.n: Any promise made in advertisements or brochures forms part of the developer's legal obligation to the buyer.

questions.q: What is the minimum required front setback for a house in an Open Market subdivision?
questions.n: 3.0 meters is the standard minimum front setback required to provide adequate space from the road.

questions.q: True or False: A developer can legally increase the price of a lot after the Contract to Sell has been signed by both parties.
questions.n: The price agreed upon in the signed contract is binding and cannot be changed unilaterally by the developer.

questions.q: Which of these is a 'mandatory' facility that must be provided in a subdivision under PD 957?
questions.n: The law requires a system for sanitary waste disposal and collection.

questions.q: What happens if a buyer stops paying because the developer failed to finish the roads on time?
o: The buyer can suspend payment after notifying the developer
The buyer must keep paying regardless of progress
The buyer will be sued for breach of contract
The buyer's payments are automatically forfeited
questions.n: PD 957 allows buyers to stop paying if the project is delayed, provided they send a notice.

questions.q: Who is responsible for paying the Real Estate Tax on a lot before it is delivered to the buyer?
questions.n: The developer or owner of the project is responsible for all taxes until the lot is turned over to the buyer.

questions.q: What is the minimum width for an 'Alley' in a PD 957 project?
questions.n: PD 957 specifies that an alley, intended for pedestrian or emergency access, must be at least 3.0 meters wide.

questions.q: In a condominium, what do you call the areas like the lobby, elevators, and roof deck?
questions.n: Common areas are shared spaces owned by all unit owners through the condominium corporation.

questions.q: What is the primary role of the DHSUD (Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development)?
o: To regulate and license subdivision and condo developers
To build all houses in the country
To collect property taxes for the city
To design the floor plans for every unit
questions.n: DHSUD ensures developers follow the law and protects the rights of the buyers.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the required pavement material for roads in an Open Market subdivision?
questions.n: The law requires durable, all-weather surfaces like concrete or asphalt for subdivision roads.

questions.q: What is the minimum floor area for a single unit in an Open Market condominium?
questions.n: The minimum floor area for a condominium unit (studio) under PD 957 is 18 square meters.

questions.q: Why is a 'Firewall' required in row house developments?
o: To make the house look taller
To provide a place for neighbors to paint murals
To support the weight of the roof
To prevent fire from spreading from one house to another
questions.n: A firewall acts as a physical barrier to contain a fire within a single unit.

questions.q: In a subdivision, what is a 'Cul-de-sac'?
o: A dead-end street with a turn-around area at the end
The main entrance of the subdivision
questions.n: It is a short street designed so that cars can turn around easily without reversing.

questions.q: What is the minimum required side setback for a residential lot?
questions.n: The standard minimum for side and rear setbacks is 2.0 meters.

questions.q: Who must sign the 'Subdivision Plan' before it is submitted to DHSUD for approval?
o: A licensed Architect or Civil Engineer
questions.n: Professional plans must be signed and sealed by the appropriate licensed professionals.

questions.q: What does 'Saleable Area' include?
questions.n: The saleable area consists of the actual land units that will be sold to individual buyers.

questions.q: How many units are typically allowed in one row of row houses before a break is required?
questions.n: Under PD 957, a cluster of row houses cannot exceed 20 units without a break or yard.

questions.q: Which of these is a requirement for a 'License to Sell' to be issued?
o: A signed contract from a contractor
A photo of the completed houses
questions.n: A developer must prove they own the land (or have the right to develop it) before they can get a license to sell it.

questions.q: What is the maximum 'Saleable Area' allowed in a subdivision project?
questions.n: The law states that at least 30% must be reserved for roads and open spaces, leaving a maximum of 70% as saleable.

questions.q: True or False: An 'Open Market' subdivision is usually more expensive than an 'Economic Housing' project.
questions.n: Open Market projects have higher technical standards and larger minimum lot sizes, making them more costly.

questions.q: What is the required thickness of a concrete road in a subdivision?
questions.n: A thickness of 150 mm (6 inches) is the standard for concrete road pavements in subdivisions.

questions.q: What happens if a developer changes the subdivision's name without DHSUD approval?
o: It is a violation of the decree
As long as the signs are pretty
questions.n: Changing names or plans without approval is a violation that can lead to fines or license suspension.

questions.q: Under PD 957, what is the 'Rounding' requirement for the curb at an intersection?
questions.n: Intersections must have a curb radius (rounding) of at least 6.0 meters for safety.

questions.q: Which document is issued by the developer to a buyer after all payments are completed?
questions.n: This final document transfers the ownership completely after full payment is made.

questions.q: What is the minimum frontage for a single detached lot in an Open Market subdivision?
questions.n: For an Open Market single detached lot, the minimum required frontage is 10.0 meters.

questions.q: True or False: A subdivision developer must provide a water system connected to a public utility or a community system.
questions.n: Access to a reliable and safe water supply is a basic mandatory requirement.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a 'Sidewalk' in a subdivision road?
o: To act as a drainage canal
questions.n: Sidewalks separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic for safety.

questions.q: What is the minimum area for a single detached lot in a Medium Cost project?
questions.n: A Medium Cost single detached lot must have a minimum area of 100 square meters.

questions.q: Which of these is considered a 'Non-Saleable' open space?
questions.n: Parks are designated open spaces that are shared by the community and cannot be sold.

questions.q: In a corner lot, what is the 'Chafer'?
o: The diagonal cut-off at the corner of the property
questions.n: A chafer (usually 4 meters) is required at intersections to improve visibility and vehicle turning.

questions.q: What is the mandatory fire-resistive rating for a firewall under PD 957?
questions.n: A firewall must be able to withstand fire for at least 2 hours to prevent it from spreading.

questions.q: What is a 'Dealer' in the context of PD 957?
o: A person or entity engaged in the business of buying and selling real estate
The person who buys the lot
questions.n: A dealer specifically buys and sells for their own account in the ordinary course of business.

questions.q: What is the maximum allowed slope (grade) for roads in a subdivision?
questions.n: The maximum allowed grade for a subdivision road is 12% to ensure vehicles can safely climb it.

questions.q: If the subdivision is 1 hectare or less, what is the required width for the Main Road?
questions.n: For projects 1 hectare or below, the main road must be at least 8.0 meters wide.

questions.q: What is the 'Performance Bond' for?
o: To pay for a celebratory party
To guarantee the completion of development works
questions.n: It ensures that if the developer goes bankrupt, there is money to finish the roads and utilities.

questions.q: True or False: A developer must provide street lighting at every intersection.
questions.n: Lighting at intersections is mandatory for the safety of both pedestrians and drivers.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT allowed as a sewage disposal method in a PD 957 project?
questions.n: This is strictly illegal and environmentally hazardous.

questions.q: What is the minimum vertical clearance for an overhead power line crossing a road?
questions.n: Power lines must be high enough to allow tall trucks and equipment to pass safely underneath.

questions.q: What is a 'Block' in subdivision planning?
o: A group of lots bounded by streets
questions.n: A block is a parcel of land surrounded by roads or other boundary features.

questions.q: What is the minimum sidewalk width for a road with a 10-meter right-of-way?
questions.n: The standard minimum for a sidewalk in most PD 957 road categories is 1.3 meters.

questions.q: How long does a 'License to Sell' remain valid?
o: For as long as the developer is alive
Until the project is completed or revoked
Only until the first unit is sold
questions.n: The license stays active as long as the project is ongoing, unless the developer violates the law.

questions.q: What is the requirement for the 'Planting Strip' on a road?
o: It must be paved with concrete
It must be planted with grass or trees
It is where the drainage pipes must be visible
It must be used for parking cars
questions.n: Planting strips are intended to provide greenery and environmental benefits along the road.

questions.q: When can a 'Certificate of Completion' be issued?
o: When all roads, utilities, and facilities are fully finished
When the first house is finished
When the developer runs out of money
When the name of the subdivision is chosen
questions.n: It is issued when the entire project infrastructure matches the approved plans.

questions.q: What is the minimum required frontage for a row house?
questions.n: For an Open Market row house, the minimum frontage is 4.0 meters.

questions.q: Why does PD 957 require 'Street Lighting' every 50 meters?
o: Because the light bulbs only last 50 meters
To make the subdivision look like a Christmas tree
To ensure visibility and safety at night
questions.n: Regularly spaced lights ensure there are no dark spots that could hide hazards or criminals.

questions.q: What is the maximum 'Block Length' before an alley or path is required?
questions.n: A block cannot exceed 400 meters in length without a path for pedestrians to cross through.

questions.q: Which of these describes a 'Semi-Detached' house?
o: A house with one side wall built on the property line shared with another unit
questions.n: Also known as a duplex, it shares one wall with a neighbor.
